STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat plate, square white plate with a rim band and flat centre.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm; this one looks medium-large, around 25 cm across.
b) Reference: the steak pieces are about 5-6 cm long. The plate spans roughly 4.5 of these lengths across its width, giving about 25-27 cm.
Final width: about 26 cm (square), so area ≈ 26² = 676 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Pizza: about 2 slices' worth of pizza (one large triangular piece folded, plus a second piece on the right). Visible area covers roughly 30% of the plate, about 200 cm². Thickness: crust and cheese layer about 1.5 cm at the thickest point (cheese and dough are stacked about 2 layers). Average thickness about 1 cm. Volume ≈ 200 × 1 = 200 ml; density ~0.8 for bread/cheese mix, so ≈ 160 g. Calibrate with bread slice (30 g per slice of 11 cm): the pizza pieces are roughly 2.5 slices of bread-like mass, about 150 g.
- Steak (sirloin-like meat, three pieces): footprint about 60 cm² total, average thickness about 1.2 cm (pieces are about 1.5-2 cm thick at most, flat-ish). Volume ≈ 70 ml, density 1.0, so ≈ 70 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer or hidden food under the toppings; the pizza is a single layer on the plate. No additional items.

STEP 5 - Energy:
- Pizza (cheese and tomato, cooked): about 260 kcal per 100 g.
- Steak (cooked beef, lean-medium): about 250 kcal per 100 g.

Totals: pizza 150 g × 2.6 = 390 kcal; steak 70 g × 2.5 = 175 kcal. Total ≈ 565 kcal, about 220 g.
